questions.q: What does this program print when it totals the array?
questions.code:
nums = [5, 10, 15, 20]
total = 0
for n in nums:
    total = total + n
print(total)
questions.feedback: The loop visits each item and adds it to the running total.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 5 — Array yard, station 1: One-dimensional arrays

questions.q: What is the difference between a procedure and a function?
options: A function returns a value to the code that called it; a procedure does not
A procedure can take parameters and a function cannot
A function can only be called once in a program
A procedure is written outside the main program and a function inside it
questions.feedback: Returning a value is the whole difference. Both can take parameters.

questions.q: Explain one advantage of using sub-programs in a large program.

markPoints.concept: the same code can be called from several places instead of being repeated
accept: reuse|reused|called|call|calls|invoked|several places|wherever|more than once|written once|without writing it again|rather than repeating
markPoints.exemplar: The same code can be called from several places instead of being written out again.

markPoints.concept: so the program is shorter and a change only has to be made in one place
accept: shorter|smaller|less code|less of it|one place|in one place|single place|single spot|one spot|only once|easier to change|easier to maintain|easier to read|one copy
markPoints.exemplar: This makes the program shorter, and a change only has to be made once.

questions.example: A sub-program can be called from several places rather than having the same lines written out again and again, which makes the program shorter and means a change only has to be made in one place.
questions.paraphrase: Code written once can be invoked wherever it is needed, so there is less of it overall and any correction is made in a single spot.
questions.feedback: Called rather than repeated, and then what that saves.

questions.q: Explain why a local variable is usually preferred to a global one.

markPoints.concept: a local variable exists only inside its own sub-program
markPoints.exemplar: A local variable exists only inside its own sub-program.

markPoints.concept: so it cannot be changed by accident somewhere else in the program
markPoints.exemplar: So no other part of the program can change it by accident.

questions.example: A local variable only exists inside the sub-program that declared it, so no other part of the program can read or change it by accident, which makes faults far easier to track down.
questions.paraphrase: Since it is confined to the routine that created it, nothing elsewhere can alter it unexpectedly, which keeps bugs contained.
questions.feedback: Scope, and then why limited scope is a good thing.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 5 — Array yard, station 4: Procedures and functions
